BiblicalUsage: Chalkeos means coppery, made of brass — and the word itself is a spelling puzzle. The Greek text behind the King James spells it chalkous, and it stands once, in the idols of gold and silver and brass that men worshipped and would not repent of.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe brass idols are the saddest kind: men make gods of metal and then worship what their own hands made.
